newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo slides past key level, Seoul slumps again.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo slides past key level, Seoul slumps again.

text.p: Tokyo stocks slid below a key psychological level on Tuesday, shrugging off record highs on Wall Street to hit a 13-month low, while labour unrest in South Korea continued to pummel Seoul shares.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average slumped 549.81 points or 2.83 percent to slide past the key 19,000 level and finish at 18,896.19 -- the lowest close since December 5, 1995.
Dealers said the market discounted a recovery in the yen against the dollar and focused instead on weakness in the Japanese economy.

"Unless (Prime Minister Ryutaro) Hashimoto proposes something specific to shore up the economy, the current situation will not change," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
Solid gains in shares in Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing's flagship Cheung Kong group, following Monday's reorganisation of the company, failed to spur Hong Kong stocks.
The Hang Seng index closed 23.77 points lower at 13,420.16.
"I think only the Cheung Kong group really performed well. The others just saw some heavy profit-taking," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Market jitters over spreading labour strikes in South Korea hammered Seoul shares, sending the composite index spiralling over 2.5 percent for the second straight day.
"Prospects look even gloomier as the strikes will spread wider into more sectors of the economy," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.

Seoul's composite index finished at 611.05, down 15.82 points. Brokers said a news conference by President Kim Young-sam made clear he would not surrender to strikers and scrap a new labour law, raising concerns of further unrest.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index ended up a mere 0.87 points at 2,246.59, surrendering morning gains in a bout of late profit taking.
Australian shares also ended down, hit by a three percent plunge in the gold sector following a slide in global bullion prices . The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished off 9.1 points at 2,400.7.
Taiwan ended up 30.27 points or 0.44 percent at 6,875.02, off a 6,897.39 high. Thai stocks rallied on a technical rebound, ending up 29.88 points, or 3.78 percent, at 820.11.
Kuala Lumpur's Composite Index rebounded from early losses, ending up 4.38 points at 1,237.50. Overseas buying pushed up Jakarta's index 6.41 points, or 0.98 percent, to 660.37 points.
Philippine shares rose for the second straight day, helped by secondliners, traders said. The main index closed up 9.10 points, or 0.29 percent, at 3,195.47 points.
Bombay shares added 12.07 points to 3,264.38, bolstered by gains in a few heavyweight stocks, while in New Zealand, the NZSE-40 capital index gained 11 points to close at 2,408.28.
February Brent crude futures were slightly lower, last trading at $24.50 a barrel on SIMEX, down six cents from London's Monday settlement.
Hong Kong gold ended at US$357.80/358.30 an ounce against New York's US$357.50/358.00 close on Friday.
At 1155 GMT the dollar was trading at 115.45/50 yen and 1.5613/20 marks.
